$comment: How a server's OperationLimits combine with this project's own (issue #139), driven through BOTH runtimes: tests/unit/test_operation_limits.py and packages/server-node/test/operation-limits.test.mjs read this file. `effective` is effectiveLimit / effective_limit: the server can only lower a project limit, and 0, a missing node or a nonsense value means it states none. `chunks` is how one logical read is split into service calls: consecutive, in order, never larger than the size in force — the sizes listed are the lengths of the requests that go on the wire. `aggregateIntervals` is how many intervals an aggregate read would ask the server to compute, which is what limits.maxHistoryValues bounds for it.

effective.name: a server that states nothing leaves ours
a higher server limit does not raise ours
a server limit of one is honoured
a negative limit is nonsense, and states nothing
a fractional limit is truncated toward zero

chunks.name: nothing to read is no request at all
exactly one request's worth is one request
one over is two, the second carrying the one
a browse detail read is three attributes a node
a size of zero still makes progress, one at a time

aggregateIntervals.name: no interval is one interval over the whole range
a partial last interval still counts
a backwards range is as many intervals as a forwards one
an empty range is still one interval
